newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says new finmin needs time to handle job.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says new finmin needs time to handle job.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Sunday that his new finance minister should be given time to do his job properly with the national economy in crisis.

He said he had confidence that Thanong Bidaya, a low-profile banker, would be able to handle the job effectively. Thanong was named on Friday to replace Amnuay Viravan who quit after differences with his political rivals in the premier's six-party coalition government.
"Thanong is new in the job and we should give him enough time to study and do his job," he told a news conference.

Chavalit also said that he would remain in overall charge of the economy while Thanong took care of the finance ministry. Thailand is undergoing its worst economic clump in over a decade with troubles in its ailing finance and property sectors.

He also said there was no need to postpone a parlimentary debate set for June 25 on the government's proposed 1997/1998 (October/September) budget next week amid a belief that the new finance minister may not be prepared to handle it.
"A man like Thanong has enough expertise and should not have problems. Some have asked me to postpone this debate on the bill but there is no need for this," he said.
